root_cause.text: The MPTCP in-kernel endpoint removal path in `net/mptcp/pm_kernel.c` failed to always return the endpoint ID to `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` for non-`SUBFLOW` endpoints, leaving an ID marked used even after the endpoint was deleted and later reused.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `__set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap)` out of the `if (ret)`/`SUBFLOW`-only handling and into the common removal path, and the CVE text says the bit “was still unset after having removed the endpoint,” causing `__mark_subflow_endp_available()` to warn when `local_addr_used` was 0 while the ID was still marked used.

intent_record.intent_summary: Stop reusing the removed address ID too early when removing an announced MPTCP address.
intent_record.what: In `mptcp_pm_remove_anno_addr()`, the `__set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap);` call was removed from the `if (ret)` block, leaving only `msk->pm.add_addr_signaled--;` before `mptcp_pm_remove_addr(msk, &list);` under the same lock.
intent_record.how: When an announced address is removed successfully, the address ID is no longer marked as immediately reusable in `id_avail_bitmap` by this path. The code still decrements the signaled address count and removes the address entry, but it avoids prematurely returning the ID to the available pool.

intent_record.intent_summary: Consolidate locked endpoint removal logic and restore availability tracking for non-subflow endpoints.
intent_record.what: The code removes two separate spin_lock_bh()/spin_unlock_bh() sections and replaces them with a single locked region around the subflow-removal and endpoint-availability update logic. Inside that region, it keeps the existing mptcp_pm_rm_subflow() call when remove_subflow is true, keeps __mark_subflow_endp_available() when the entry has MPTCP_PM_ADDR_FLAG_SUBFLOW, and adds an else branch that calls __set_bit(addr->id, msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap) with a comment indicating this is for Signal or MPC endpoints.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the subflow removal and endpoint ID bookkeeping now happen under one consistent lock, preventing races between removal and availability updates. It also ensures that non-subflow endpoints explicitly have their endpoint ID marked available again, which restores ID reuse for Signal or MPC endpoints and avoids leaving those IDs incorrectly unavailable.

candidates.rationale: This is part of the endpoint removal path where the code clears the active endpoint ID, but in the pre-fix logic there is no corresponding restoration of the removed non-SUBFLOW endpoint's ID back into the availability bitmap, which allows the ID to remain marked as used after deletion.

This is the actual removal operation for the announced MPTCP address; the vulnerable behavior is that for non-SUBFLOW endpoints this removal path did not always return the endpoint ID to msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap afterward, leading to stale ID allocation state.

This locked removal helper is part of the endpoint deletion flow. The bug is tied to inconsistent cleanup in the removal path: subflow handling had availability restoration elsewhere, while non-SUBFLOW endpoints lacked equivalent bitmap reset logic.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the actual announced-address removal call in the kernel endpoint deletion path. The root cause is that, for non-SUBFLOW endpoints, this path did not always return the removed endpoint ID to msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap after deletion, leaving the ID stale and unavailable for reuse.

This removal helper is part of the same endpoint-deletion flow. The bug is in the inconsistent cleanup logic around deletion: subflow handling and non-SUBFLOW handling diverged, and the non-SUBFLOW path failed to restore endpoint ID availability after removal.

This conditional is where the active endpoint ID is cleared during locked endpoint removal. In the pre-fix logic, this clearing did not guarantee that a deleted non-SUBFLOW endpoint ID was also returned to the availability bitmap, which is the stated root cause.

commit 8617e85e04bd08c6c6aa24c832f9bec10bf76648
Author: Matthieu Baerts (NGI0) <matttbe@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Mar 7 12:21:58 2025 +0100

    mptcp: pm: split in-kernel PM specific code
    
    Before this patch, the PM code was dispersed in different places:
    
    - pm.c had common code for all PMs
    
    - pm_netlink.c was supposed to be about the in-kernel PM, but also had
      exported common Netlink helpers, NL events for PM userspace daemons,
      etc. quite confusing.
    
    To
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present and already handled correctly in this snippet. The root cause was failing to return an endpoint ID to `msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap` when a non-SUBFLOW endpoint is deleted. In this code, deletion explicitly clears the per-net ID bitmap entry at removal time: `__clear_bit(entry->addr.id, pernet->id_bitmap);` in `mptcp_pm_nl_del_addr_doit()`, and for active sockets it also returns the socket-local ID in the removal path for subflow endpoints via `__mark_subflow_endp_available(msk, list.ids[0]);`. The helper `__mark_subflow_endp_available()` does `__test_and_set_bit(..., msk->pm.id_avail_bitmap)` and decrements `local_addr_used`, ensuring the endpoint ID is returned to availability. Because the fix is already present in the removal logic and the bitmap is cleared on delete, this commit version is not bug-introducing for the described root cause.

Since the code shown already contains the bitmap restoration logic, the vulnerable construct is absent here and the fix is present.
